Rules / Modernization

SK1003 Use a field-backed property

A private backing field is used exclusively inside one property's get and set accessors.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 14.0
Since1.3

Why

C# 14's field keyword preserves custom accessor logic while letting the compiler own backing storage. The fix removes the private declaration and replaces only references proven to belong to this property.

Example

Instead of:

private int count; public int Count { get => count; set => count = System.Math.Max(0, value); }

Write:

public int Count { get => field; set => field = System.Math.Max(0, value); }

When it does not fire

Only non-virtual class properties with explicit get and set bodies and a same-type private, non-readonly, non-volatile, uninitialized field are supported. Partial containing types, directives, field comments/attributes, property attributes, initializers, generic type-parameter storage, non-nullable reference storage, other consumers, other-instance accesses, nameof, ref escapes, caller-expression capture, nested functions and existing field identifiers are excluded. C# 14 is required. Both accessors must use the field; types with explicit layout or Serializable attributes are excluded. Reflection and serializers depending on the private field's name/layout are outside the proof.
